Code and the constitution are open-sourced.

AI.tldr: C-Guard is a constitution-grid framework for efficient RL-based safety guard training that addresses conflicting objectives (catching harm vs. avoiding over-refusal). It uses C-LIM, a learnability score, to strategically prune, densify, amend, or expand training data cells, eliminating dead-weight data before training and improving learning impact from 0.733 to 0.80.
AI.motivation: RL alignment faces conflicting objectives—safety guards must catch real harm while not refusing benign prompts. Training data-efficiently under this conflict is hard: over-refusal improves (22.4%→12.8%) but under-refusal on adversarial attacks silently worsens (0.27→0.33), motivating a smarter data generation and curation strategy.
AI.method: The authors propose C-Guard, a constitution-grid instrument for generating RL training data, paired with C-LIM, a per-cell learnability score that decides each grid cell's action: prune, densify, amend, or expand. C-LIM identifies dead-weight data regions (e.g., 187 untargeted rows with zero gain) before any training budget is spent.
AI.result: C-LIM flagged 187 untargeted rows that had bought zero gain pre-training. The method lifted the same region's learning impact from 0.733 to 0.80. Over-refusal dropped from 22.4% to 12.8%, while under-refusal on adversarial attacks was addressed (0.27→0.33 baseline).
AI.conclusion: The C-Guard framework with C-LIM enables data-efficient RL safety training by preemptively identifying and restructuring low-value training data. Code and constitution are open-sourced.

title: Ekova: A Personality-Support Agent for Self-Discovery Dialogue
comment: Accepted to the COLM 2026 Lifelong Agents Workshop
summary: Emotional Support (ES) systems have long optimized a single objective: alleviating the user's emotional distress in the moment. We argue that a complementary need, helping users see themselves more clearly, defines a distinct paradigm we call Personality Support (PS). PS is not counseling or clinical intervention: it targets cognitive clarity and self-articulation, not symptom relief or diagnosis. We instantiate this paradigm in three layers. First, we present DSD, a Chinese self-discovery PS Dataset of 8,590 samples collected through real longitudinal interaction across five minimal units, Coach, Warm, Tsukkomi, Real, and Gonzo. Second, we build DeepSupport, a multi-persona PS system trained with OrthoTune, a PS-tailored framework with style-specific adapters and a style-consistency regularizer. Third, we unify the five DeepSupport personas into Ekova, a persistent personality-support agent with a unified cross-session memory layer, supporting both adaptive routing and user-customized persona selection. Experiments show that OrthoTune-trained models outperform all baselines with an average relative gain of 16.3% across all metrics over the strongest prompt-based baseline. Code is available at https://github.com/Yukyin/Ekova.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Personality Support (PS), a new paradigm distinct from emotional support, focusing on cognitive clarity and self-articulation. It contributes a Chinese self-discovery dataset (DSD), a multi-persona PS system (DeepSupport) trained with OrthoTune, and Ekova, a unified persistent agent with cross-session memory. OrthoTune-trained models outperform baselines by 16.3% on average.
AI.motivation: Emotional Support systems have traditionally focused solely on alleviating immediate emotional distress. The authors identify an unmet, complementary need: helping users gain cognitive clarity and articulate their self-understanding. This defines the new paradigm of Personality Support (PS), which is explicitly not counseling or clinical intervention — it targets self-clarity rather than symptom relief or diagnosis.
AI.method: The work is structured in three layers: (1) DSD Dataset: 8,590 Chinese self-discovery PS samples collected via longitudinal real interactions across five minimal persona units — Coach, Warm, Tsukkomi, Real, and Gonzo. (2) DeepSupport: a multi-persona PS system trained with OrthoTune, a PS-tailored training framework featuring style-specific adapters and a style-consistency regularizer. (3) Ekova: a persistent personality-support agent that unifies all five DeepSupport personas, incorporating a unified cross-session memory layer that enables both adaptive routing and user-customized persona selection.
AI.result: OrthoTune-trained models outperform all baselines, achieving an average relative gain of 16.3% across all evaluation metrics compared to the strongest prompt-based baseline.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes Personality Support as a viable and valuable paradigm complementary to Emotional Support. The three-layer instantiation — DSD dataset, OrthoTune training framework with DeepSupport, and the Ekova agent — demonstrates that PS systems can effectively enhance users' cognitive clarity and self-articulation. The significant performance gains validate the OrthoTune approach, and the open-sourced code facilitates further research in this direction.
